correctness.rationale: Every printed hypothesis of Theorem 2.6 is satisfied by the explicit \(\mathbb C^2\) example. The source threshold is \(8<16\), but one allowed partition has coefficient energy \(2|f_1|^2\) and therefore vanishes at \(e_2\) while \(\|K^*e_2\|^2=1/16\). The repaired estimate follows by applying the frame and Bessel inequalities after taking the square root of the coefficient-energy sum.

value.rationale: The error invalidates the qualitative conclusion of a general two-operator preservation theorem, not merely an advertised constant. Scaling K by a small scalar makes the printed threshold artificially permissive, while the square-root repair restores the correct homogeneity. The counterexample is finite-dimensional, exact, and uses only a coordinate frame and a permutation.
